extraction.name: Stanford Question Answering Dataset (SQuAD)
extraction.description: A reading comprehension dataset of 100,000+ crowdworker-written questions on Wikipedia articles, where each answer is a text span from the corresponding passage.
extraction.creator: Pranav Rajpurkar, Jian Zhang, Konstantin Lopyrev, Percy Liang
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was collected in three stages: curating Wikipedia passages, crowdsourcing question-answer pairs on those passages, and collecting additional answers for development and test questions from crowdworkers.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: In the additional answer collection, if a question could not be answered by a span in the paragraph, workers submitted it without marking an answer; 2.6% of questions were marked unanswerable by at least one additional crowdworker.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw/source data consisted of English Wikipedia articles and their paragraphs. The authors used Project Nayuki's Wikipedia internal PageRanks to select from the top 10,000 articles, sampled 536 articles, and extracted paragraphs while removing images, figures, tables, and short paragraphs.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Crowdworkers created question-answer pairs for each paragraph and additional workers provided extra answer spans for dev/test. Workers asked and answered up to 5 questions per paragraph, entered questions in text fields, highlighted answer spans, were given sample paragraphs and examples of good/bad questions and answers, were encouraged to paraphrase rather than copy, and copy-paste was disabled. In the secondary task, workers selected the shortest answer span or marked the question unanswerable.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Daemo platform with Amazon Mechanical Turk as backend
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Additional answers were collected to estimate human performance and improve evaluation robustness; 2.6% of dev/test questions were marked unanswerable by at least one additional worker.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: Up to 5 question-answer annotations per paragraph; at least 2 additional answers per question in development and test sets
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Crowdworkers located in the United States or Canada, with at least 97% HIT acceptance rate and a minimum of 1000 HITs
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset includes ambiguous examples and reflects biases from crowdsourced span-based question answering over Wikipedia articles. The answer distribution is uneven across types, and all sampled examples showed lexical or syntactic divergence between questions and answer sentences.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is limited to questions on Wikipedia articles with answers restricted to text spans from passages, making it more constrained than free-form or more interpretative reading comprehension tasks. There are also annotation and modeling limitations: some questions are ambiguous or lack unique answers, and many correct answers are not constituency parse constituents, imposing an accuracy ceiling for the methods described.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for training and evaluating machine reading comprehension/question answering systems, particularly span-based answer selection from passages.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The paper identifies a versioned release (SQuAD v1.0 and v1.1) and states the dataset is freely available online, but does not provide an explicit maintenance, update timeframe, maintainer, or deprecation policy.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Randomly sampled 536 articles from the top 10,000 English Wikipedia articles and randomly partitioned articles into training (80%), development (10%), and test (10%) sets.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Extracted individual paragraphs from articles, removed images, figures, and tables, and discarded paragraphs shorter than 500 characters.

name.evidence: We present the Stanford Question Answering Dataset (SQuAD)

description.evidence: a new reading comprehension dataset consisting of 100,000+ questions posed by crowdworkers on a set of Wikipedia articles, where the answer to each question is a segment of text from the corresponding reading passage

url.evidence: The dataset is freely available at https://stanford-qa.com

creator.evidence: Pranav Rajpurkar and Jian Zhang and Konstantin Lopyrev and Percy Liang

datePublished.evidence: Over the last four months (since June 2016), we have witnessed significant improvements

inLanguage.evidence: consisting of questions posed by crowdworkers on a set of Wikipedia articles

isLiveDataset.evidence: Over the last four months (since June 2016), we have witnessed significant improvements from more sophisticated neural network-based models. For example, Wang and Jiang (2016) obtained 70.3% F1 on SQuAD v1.1

rai:dataCollection.evidence: We collect our dataset in three stages: curating passages, crowdsourcing question-answers on those passages, and obtaining additional answers.

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: Next, we employed crowdworkers to create questions.

rai:dataCollectionMissingData.evidence: If a question was not answerable by a span in the paragraph, workers were asked to submit the question without marking an answer. Over the development and test sets, 2.6% of questions were marked unanswerable by at least one of the additional crowdworkers.

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: we used Project Nayuki’s Wikipedia’s internal PageRanks to obtain the top 10000 articles of English Wikipedia, from which we sampled 536 articles uniformly at random. From each of these articles, we extracted individual paragraphs, stripping away images, figures, tables, and discarding paragraphs shorter than 500 characters.

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: “On each paragraph, crowdworkers were tasked with asking and answering up to 5 questions on the content of that paragraph. The questions had to be entered in a text field, and the answers had to be highlighted in the paragraph... tasks contained a sample paragraph, and examples of good and bad questions and answers... crowdworkers were encouraged to ask questions in their own words... disabling copy-paste functionality... In the secondary answer generation task, each crowdworker was shown only the questions along with the paragraphs of an article, and asked to select the shortest span in the paragraph that answered the question. If a question was not answerable by a span in the paragraph, workers were asked to submit the question without marking an answer.”

rai:dataAnnotationPlatform.evidence: “We used the Daemo platform (Gaikwad et al., 2015), with Amazon Mechanical Turk as its backend.”

rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis.evidence: “To get an indication of human performance on SQuAD and to make our evaluation more robust, we obtained at least 2 additional answers for each question in the development and test sets... Over the development and test sets, 2.6% of questions were marked unanswerable by at least one of the additional crowdworkers.”

rai:annotationsPerItem.evidence: “On each paragraph, crowdworkers were tasked with asking and answering up to 5 questions on the content of that paragraph.” and “we obtained at least 2 additional answers for each question in the development and test sets.”

rai:annotatorDemographics.evidence: “Crowdworkers were required to have a 97% HIT acceptance rate, a minimum of 1000 HITs, and be located in the United States or Canada.”

rai:dataBiases.evidence: "The results show that all examples have some sort of lexical or syntactic divergence between the question and the answer in the passage."

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: "While questions with span-based answers are more constrained than the more interpretative questions found in more advanced standardized tests"

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: "To address the need for a large and high-quality reading comprehension dataset, we present the Stanford Question Answering Dataset v1.0 (SQuAD)"

rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan.evidence: "we present the Stanford Question Answering Dataset v1.0 (SQuAD), freely available at https://stanford-qa.com"

rai:dataManipulationProtocol.evidence: we used Project Nayuki’s Wikipedia’s internal PageRanks to obtain the top 10000 articles of English Wikipedia, from which we sampled 536 articles uniformly at random... We partitioned the articles randomly into a training set (80%), a development set (10%), and a test set (10%).

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: From each of these articles, we extracted individual paragraphs, stripping away images, figures, tables, and discarding paragraphs shorter than 500 characters.
